questions.prompt: A pair \((A, C)\) is observable when
options: a finite record of the output determines the initial state
some input can drive every state to the origin
every eigenvalue of \(A\) has a negative real part
\(C\) is a row of ones
questions.explanation: Observability is about the sensor, not the actuator. The output over an interval fixes \(x(0)\) precisely when the stacked matrix of \(C, CA, \ldots\) has full rank. Reachability is the input test. Stability is the eigenvalue test. A row of ones is one particular \(C\), not the definition.

questions.prompt: For \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -3 & -4 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(C = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\), the absolute value of \(\det\begin{bmatrix} C \\ CA \end{bmatrix}\) is
questions.explanation: \(CA = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\), so the stacked matrix is the identity and its determinant has absolute value 1. A determinant of 0 would mean a hidden mode. The trace of \(A\), which is \(-4\), is not this determinant.

questions.prompt: For \(A = \mathrm{diag}(-2, -5)\) and \(C = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\), the rank of the observability matrix is
questions.explanation: \(CA = \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\). Both rows are multiples of \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\), so the rank is 1, not 2. The second mode is invisible. Rank 0 would require \(C = 0\).
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 130" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>a stacked output matrix with a zero column</title><text x="28" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">[</text><text x="168" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">]</text><text x="98" y="58" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">1   0</text><text x="98" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">-2   0</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A 2 by 2 matrix whose second column is zero.

questions.prompt: Let \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(C = \begin{bmatrix} c & d \end{bmatrix}\). Write \(\det\begin{bmatrix} C \\ CA \end{bmatrix}\) in the names c and d.
questions.explanation: \(CA = \begin{bmatrix} d & c \end{bmatrix}\), so the determinant is \(c^2 - d^2\). The sum \(c^2 + d^2\) would be the determinant of a different stacking, with a sign error in the second row. The product \(cd\) is one entry, not the determinant.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 130" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>a full-rank stacked output matrix</title><text x="28" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">[</text><text x="168" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">]</text><text x="98" y="58" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">1   0</text><text x="98" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">0   1</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A 2 by 2 matrix with ones on the diagonal and zeros off it.

questions.prompt: A three-state \(A = \mathrm{diag}(-1,-2,-3)\) is measured by \(C = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\). How many states are unobservable?
questions.explanation: The rows \(C\), \(CA\), and \(CA^2\) are \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\), \(\begin{bmatrix} -1 & 0 & -3 \end{bmatrix}\), and \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 9 \end{bmatrix}\). The middle column is zero, and the other two columns are independent, so the rank is 2. One state is hidden. Reporting 3 counts every state as hidden. Reporting 0 treats a nonzero \(C\) as a full test.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 130" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>a stacked output matrix with a zero column</title><text x="28" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">[</text><text x="168" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">]</text><text x="98" y="58" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">1   0</text><text x="98" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">-2   0</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A 2 by 2 matrix whose second column is zero.

questions.prompt: Put these steps in the order you would use to test observability.
questions.explanation: The rows are the output map and its images under \(A\). Stacking them is what makes one matrix. The rank is the number of independent output directions. Full rank, equal to \(n\), is the test. Declaring observability from a nonzero \(C\) skips the rank.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 280 210" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>two output directions</title><line x1="46" y1="161.7" x2="250" y2="161.7"/><polygon points="250,161.7 243.6,164.4 243.6,159" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="60.1" y1="176" x2="60.1" y2="28"/><polygon points="60.1,28 62.8,34.4 57.3,34.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="248" y="175.7" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">x1</text><text x="66.1" y="30" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">x2</text><line x1="60.1" y1="161.7" x2="235.9" y2="140"/><polygon points="235.9,140 229.9,143.5 229.2,138.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="243.9" y="132" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">C</text><line x1="60.1" y1="161.7" x2="104" y2="42.3"/><polygon points="104,42.3 104.4,49.3 99.2,47.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="112" y="34.3" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">CA</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: Two arrows from the origin pointing in different directions.
steps: Form the rows C, CA, and so on up to C A to the n-1.
Stack those rows into one matrix.
Compute the rank of that matrix.
Call the pair observable only when the rank equals the number of states.

questions.prompt: A calculation looks at \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\) as an observability matrix. One step is wrong.
questions.explanation: Proportional rows are rank 1, so one direction never reaches the sensor. A nonzero row only shows that something is measured. The first two steps read the matrix correctly, and the last step is the reason the rank has to be \(n\) before every mode can be estimated.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 130" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>a stacked output matrix with a zero column</title><text x="28" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">[</text><text x="168" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">]</text><text x="98" y="58" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">1   0</text><text x="98" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">-2   0</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A 2 by 2 matrix whose second column is zero.
steps: The two rows are proportional: the second is twice the first.
Proportional rows mean the rank is 1, short of a two-state system.
A nonzero first row means every mode is visible at the output, so the pair is observable.
An observer gain exists for every mode only when the rank equals the number of states.
reasons: A nonzero row is not full rank. Proportional rows leave one mode hidden.
Proportional rows have rank 2, so the third step is the one that is right.
The first row being nonzero already contradicts the claim that the rows are proportional.

questions.prompt: Observability of \((A, C)\) is the same rank condition as reachability of
options: \((A, B)\) for every \(B\)
\((C, A)\), with the factors swapped and not transposed
questions.explanation: The observability matrix of \((A, C)\) is the transpose of the controllability matrix of \((A^T, C^T)\). Rank is unchanged by transpose, so the tests match. \((A, C)\) is not a reachability pair. Reachability of \((A, B)\) is a different matrix. Swapping to \((C, A)\) without the transpose is not the dual.

questions.prompt: Which of these pairs are observable?
options: \(A = \mathrm{diag}(-2,-5)\), \(C = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\)
\(A = \mathrm{diag}(-2,-5)\), \(C = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\)
\(A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 \end{bmatrix}\), \(C = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\)
\(A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\), \(C = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\)
questions.explanation: A diagonal pair is observable when every mode has a nonzero entry in \(C\). The row \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\) misses the second mode, and \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\) sees both. The companion pair with \(C = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\) has observability matrix equal to the identity. Measuring only the velocity of a double integrator leaves the position as a hidden integrator: \(CA = 0\).
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 130" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>a full-rank stacked output matrix</title><text x="28" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">[</text><text x="168" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">]</text><text x="98" y="58" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">1   0</text><text x="98" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">0   1</text></svg>

questions.prompt: For \(A = \mathrm{diag}(-1, -4)\) and \(C = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\), the absolute value of the observability determinant is
questions.explanation: \(CA = \begin{bmatrix} -2 & -20 \end{bmatrix}\). The determinant is \(2(-20) - 5(-2) = -30\), absolute value 30. The product of the \(C\) entries, 10, drops the images under \(A\). The sum of the diagonal entries of \(A\), \(-5\), is the trace.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 130" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>a stacked 2 by 2 output matrix</title><text x="28" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">[</text><text x="168" y="78" text-anchor="middle" font-size="28" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">]</text><text x="98" y="58" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">2   5</text><text x="98" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">-2   -20</text></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A 2 by 2 matrix with first row 2, 5 and second row -2, -20.

questions.prompt: A mode that does not appear in any row \(C, CA, \ldots\)
options: is always unstable
can be moved by output injection without changing \(C\)
can be removed from the input-output map even though it is still an eigenvalue of \(A\)
raises the rank of the observability matrix
questions.explanation: A hidden mode is invisible at \(y\), so a minimal input-output model deletes it. It remains an eigenvalue of the larger \(A\). Nothing about the rank test forces it to be unstable. Output injection \(A - LC\) cannot move a mode that \(C\) does not see, and a missing direction lowers the rank rather than raising it.

questions.prompt: Observable canonical form is worth building because, when nothing has cancelled,
options: every realization in that form has a singular observability matrix
the transfer function gains an extra pole
reachability is automatic even if \(B = 0\)
the observability matrix is full rank, so an observer gain can be designed
questions.explanation: The form puts the output map in a coordinate system whose observability matrix is triangular and invertible, as long as no mode was cancelled. A cancelled mode is exactly a drop in rank. The transfer function is unchanged by the coordinate change. Reachability is a property of \(B\), not of this form.
